CHANGELOG: collapse to single v1.0.0 release entry

The toolkit is launching alongside the Claude Design article today —
there is no public v1.0 baseline that readers will remember. The
previous two-version structure (v1.0.0 = 6 files, v1.1.0 = 17 files)
made the repo look like 'you missed the first release' to anyone
landing here cold from the article.

Collapsed to a single v1.0.0 entry that describes what is in this
release in present tense: 9 prompts + 6 references + cheatsheet +
license. Grouped by what they do, not by when they were added.

Kept the risk note (research-preview caveat + portability argument
for if Anthropic ever deprecates Claude Design) — that ages well
regardless of release-history framing.

Update article URL to canonical /p/claude-design

The newsletter post slug landed as /p/claude-design (not the
provisional /p/pm-guide-claude-design). Updated all 4 references
in README.md and CHEATSHEET.md so links point to the live post.

README + CHEATSHEET: surface the new commerce / research / changelog files

Round-2 added 14_commerce_page (Omar's e-commerce gap), 15_research_
prototype (Hannah's research gap), and CHANGELOG.md (Elena's version-
ing gap) — but the front-door files (README quickstart table, file
inventory, CHEATSHEET use-case map) still pointed only at the
original 13 files. Linking them in so they are discoverable.

README updates:
- Quickstart table: added rows for commerce + research prototypes
  with timing estimates.
- File inventory tables: added 14, 15, and CHANGELOG with one-line
  descriptions matching the file's actual scope.

CHEATSHEET updates:
- Quickstart-by-use-case mini-table: added commerce + research rows.

Add CHANGELOG.md — version history + Claude Design risk note

Persona-18 (Elena, second-time founder, Tel Aviv) flagged the lack of
versioning. As a veteran she has been burned by tools that change
their API without warning — wanted to know what version of Claude
Design these prompts target, and what to do when it changes.

Ships:
- v1.0.0 baseline (the original 6 files from the article release)
- v1.1.0 round-2 expansion (the 11 new files + 6 updated files
  shipped in this batch)
- 'Tested against Claude Design Research Preview, April 2026'
  version pin so future readers know what was current
- A risk note at the bottom: what to do if Anthropic ships a
  breaking change (check changelog → open issue), and the portab-
  ility argument (the underlying CSS / animation patterns are
  stack-agnostic and transfer to v0, Bolt, Lovable if Claude Design
  is ever deprecated)

Format inspired by Keep a Changelog — Added / Changed sections,
semver-style version numbers.

Add 15_research_prototype: unmoderated usability test prototype

Persona-16 (Hannah, researcher-turned-PM, Stockholm) flagged that no
prompt addressed actual user research needs. Stakeholder prototype
(08) is for stakeholders giving you a yes/no — not for real users
completing tasks while you watch from a distance.

Ships a research-specific prototype structure:
- Welcome screen with all tasks listed up front (participant sees
  the full scope before starting)
- The product flow as it would appear in production with NO reviewer
  hints, NO arrows, NO 'click here' cheats — point is to see if they
  figure it out
- Persistent task sidebar with completion checkmarks + a 'I am stuck
  — skip this task' link (real research lets people give up;
  without skip, false-positive completions wreck your data)
- Auto-completion detection wired up via JavaScript watching for the
  implicit success state of each task
- Exit survey with 4 standard questions (1-5 ease scale, open-text
  confusion moment, 0-10 NPS, open-text other) — no separate
  Typeform needed

Includes a companion test-plan template to paste alongside the URL
when sending to Maze, UserTesting, Lyssna, or a recruiter — covers
screening criteria, tasks, and 'what I am specifically watching for'
prompts for the moderator.

Includes a comparison table showing exactly what differs between
stakeholder prototype (08) and research prototype (15).

Add 14_commerce_page: PDP / cart / checkout flow for retail PMs

Persona-19 (Omar, e-commerce PM, Cairo) flagged that every prompt in
the toolkit targets marketing or onboarding surfaces. Retail PMs had
no entry point — asking the default prompt for 'a product page'
returns a marketing landing page with a 'Buy now' CTA, not a real
PDP with variants, inventory states, and add-to-cart flows.

Ships a 3-screen commerce flow:
- PDP with tactile variant selectors (color swatches + size buttons,
  never dropdowns), quantity stepper, inventory states (in stock /
  low stock / out of stock with notify-me), sticky add-to-bag CTA
- Mini-cart slide-out with promo code, free-shipping progress bar,
  trust signals
- Single-page checkout (multi-step converts worse) with express
  payments (Apple Pay / Shop Pay), real address autocomplete,
  card-type detection while typing, order confirmation with
  CSS-only checkmark animation

Includes RTL support refinement prompt for MENA shipping (logical
CSS properties, dir='auto', mirrored directional icons, currency
symbol position).

Includes 3 refinement variants: express checkout wiring, subscribe-
and-save toggle, post-purchase upsell.

Explicit anti-patterns: no exit-intent modals, no countdown timers,
no '27 people are viewing this' fake social proof — modern brands
skip these.

12_error_recovery: add WCAG/a11y failure recovery + reduced-motion fix

Persona-20 (Chen, a11y consultant + PM, Vancouver) flagged the
absence of accessibility recovery prompts. The original 12 failures
covered visual and behavioral bugs but skipped the entire WCAG
failure surface — which is the single most common reason a 'finished'
prototype gets bounced from review.

Added two new entries:

#12 Accessibility scan fails — covers contrast, focus states, alt
text, form labels, heading hierarchy, keyboard nav, reduced motion.
Includes a general 'fix everything' prompt and a targeted prompt for
the most common subcase (low-contrast text on video backgrounds, with
two design-preserving remediation options).

#13 prefers-reduced-motion is not respected — covers the global media
query plus video-pause-on-mount with opt-in 'Play background' button,
plus reducing the word-by-word blur animation to a 200ms opacity
fade.

Renumbered the meta-pattern entry to #14 and updated the file header
count.

11_claude_code_handoff: add security baseline + i18n + bundle budget

Persona-12 (Dev, technical PM at dev tools, Bangalore) flagged 3 gaps:
- No security checklist (XSS, CSRF, secret handling) — a generated
  prototype handed off without sanitization can ship dangerouslySet-
  InnerHTML or inline event handlers straight to prod.
- No i18n baseline — handed-off code routinely hard-codes strings
  and CSS direction, blocking shipping in MENA, EU, and APAC.
- No bundle budget guidance — Claude Code agents will happily npm-
  install a 200KB date library to format one timestamp.

Added 3 new template sections (Security Baseline, Internationali-
zation, Bundle Size Budget) and updated the Definition of Done
checklist with: bundle size delta, i18n string extraction, security
patterns review, prefers-reduced-motion verification.

These additions mean the README hand-off captures the production
baseline most engineering teams expect — fewer PR comments, faster
merge.

10_clarifying_questions: add anti-copy taboos to the 30-second template

Persona-15 (Benoit, designer-turned-PM advisor, Paris) noted that the
30-second template handled what to DO but not what to NOT do, lin-
guistically. Visual taboos were covered; copy taboos were not. Result:
first-generation copy still came back with 'leverage', 'seamless',
and 'Get Started'.

Added two new template fields ('Words we never use' + 'CTA
vocabulary') and a full anti-copy reference list with 4 categories:
buzzword bingo (the always-ban list), generic CTA verbs (with
alternatives), filler phrases, and brand-specific ban list (the most
powerful — what your competitors overuse and you specifically reject).

Pasted into a clarifying answer, this drops first-generation copy
revision cycles by ~30% based on Aakash's testing notes.

05_design_system: add 3 alt typography sets + WCAG ratios on dark tokens

Persona-15 (Benoit, designer-turned-PM advisor, Paris) flagged the
aesthetic monoculture: every output is dark-cinematic or clean-SaaS.
Real PM work spans a wider range. Added 3 typography sets with
distinct vibes:
- Warm Consumer (Fraunces + Inter, off-white bg, terracotta accent)
  → newsletters, reading apps, journaling tools
- Retro Terminal (JetBrains Mono headings + lowercase + cursor blink)
  → CLI tools, dev infra, anything CLI-adjacent
- Playful Consumer (Funnel Display + bright non-neutrals, generous
  border-radius) → social, games, creator tools

Persona-20 (Chen, a11y consultant + PM, Vancouver) flagged the lack
of WCAG contrast guidance on the dark color tokens. Added inline
contrast-ratio annotations on every text token (--text 19.8:1 AAA,
--text-muted ~10.5:1 AA, --text-dim ~4.6:1 large-text-only) plus an
explicit warning that --text-dim must not be used on body text.

04_animated_showcase: add no-video fallback + prefers-reduced-motion

Persona-2 (Marcus, solo founder, NYC) flagged that the Mux/Cloudflare
hosting step is a hidden cost and time tax for someone without a
video ready. Added a CSS-only fallback using animated gradients,
blurred orbs, and SVG noise texture — ships in 6 minutes instead of
45, no hosting dependency, also works where autoplay video is
blocked (iOS low-power, some CMS embeds).

Persona-20 (Chen, a11y consultant + PM, Vancouver) flagged that zero
prompts handle prefers-reduced-motion. A cinematic page with blur,
stagger, scale, and autoplay video can trigger migraines and
vestibular responses — WCAG 2.1 requires an opt-out. Added a refine-
ment prompt that wraps all animations in @media (prefers-reduced-
motion: reduce), pauses the background video, replaces word-by-word
blur with opacity-only fade, and offers a 'Play background' button
for users who do want the motion back.

Fix article URL: point to specific post, not newsletter homepage

All 4 references previously pointed to www.news.aakashg.com (the
homepage), which sends readers to the latest post — not the Claude
Design article. Updated to the canonical post URL:
https://www.news.aakashg.com/p/pm-guide-claude-design

Affects README.md (3 refs) and CHEATSHEET.md (1 ref).

03_feature_flow: prevent example-block leak + add i18n refinement prompt

Persona-5 (Jules, Staff PM enterprise, Berlin) flagged that the
inline 'Example: "..."' italicized blocks inside the prompt will
leak into the output if a PM forgets to scrub them. First session
outputs were hybrid hiring-example / PM's-actual-product Frankenstein
flows. Added a bold warning callout at the top with scrub instruction
before Send.

Persona-19 (Omar, e-commerce PM, Cairo) flagged the lack of i18n
guidance and RTL support — a blocker for MENA / European teams that
ship multilingual products. Added a copy-paste refinement prompt that
wraps user-facing copy in t('namespace.key') i18n functions, extracts
to en.json, and handles RTL layouts via dir="auto" + logical CSS
properties + rtl:rotate-180 on directional icons.

02_product_launch: add analytics hooks + ESP integration variants

Persona-6 (Kenji, Growth PM at consumer app, Tokyo) flagged the lack
of analytics wiring guidance. A launch page without event tracking
is half-shipped — you cannot measure what worked. Added 3 analytics
hook variants (PostHog, Segment, GA4) as copy-paste follow-up prompts
that wire events onto the existing page without a re-render.

Persona-7 (Sarah, PMM, London) flagged the lack of email service
integration guidance. Most PMMs use ConvertKit or HubSpot; the old
prompt produced a disconnected <input> with no delivery path. Added
3 ESP integration variants (ConvertKit, HubSpot Forms, Resend/self-
rolled) with success and error state specifications.

01_investor_demo: add board CTA variant + WCAG contrast guidance

Persona-1 (Priya, Sr PM at Series B fintech, SF) flagged that 'See
the Product' + 'Book a Demo' reads consumer-facing when sent to a
board. Added a CTA-swap variant: 'Read the board memo' + 'Book 15
min with the founder' — matches how boards actually engage.

Persona-20 (Chen, a11y consultant + PM, Vancouver) flagged that
white/55 and white/60 body copy fails WCAG 2.1 AA on ~half of Kling
video backgrounds. Added a 4-step pre-share accessibility checklist
with concrete remediation steps (bump white/55 to white/75 globally
via Tweaks — free, one-click) and the option to increase the video
dark overlay from bg-black/25 to bg-black/40 for bright frames.

06_pm_tips: align token costs with article + add data-privacy caveat

Persona-20 (Chen, a11y consultant + PM, Vancouver) flagged that the
old '$10-20 per page' number contradicts the article's stated '$2-7
per artifact'. Updated to match: $2-7 for first pass, $10-20 only for
heavy sessions with 3+ refinement rounds.

Persona-13 (Amina, Product Ops at 1000-person SaaS, Lagos) flagged
the lack of data-privacy guidance. Ops teams at larger orgs cannot
roll Claude Design out without a written 'what not to paste' rule.
Added section 7 covering PII, secrets, Figma screenshots, and
production data policies. Ships the minimum governance bar that an
ops lead can forward to security without embarrassment.

Add CHEATSHEET.md — printable 1-pager ('tape above your monitor')

Mirrors the 'Printable Summary' graphic from the article but as a
dense markdown reference. Captures: the 4 Claude Design tabs and
when to use each, the context-attachment options, the Tweaks/Edit/
Comments modality order, the 5 skills, tool-fit vs. Figma/v0/Stitch,
export paths, token budget, and a quickstart table by use case.

Designed to be kept open in a second tab during any Claude Design
session.

Add 13_internal_tool: admin / ops dashboard prompt

Most-skipped use case in the original article coverage. Every prompt
in the toolkit targeted marketing or onboarding surfaces — landing
pages, waitlists, investor demos. Platform PMs, API PMs, and ops PMs
had no starting point for the tools their teams open 30x a day.

Ships: a prompt that inverts the marketing-page defaults. Information
density over whitespace, keyboard-first navigation (J/K/Cmd-K),
command palette, detail pane, bulk actions, production-realistic
sample data (ULIDs, relative timestamps, edge-case statuses). Plus
refinement prompts for environment safety (PROD vs STAGING visual
indicators) and keyboard shortcut reference modal.

Add 12_error_recovery: 12 common failures with copy-paste fix prompts

Most Claude Design failures fall into a small set of patterns. PMs
were rebuilding from scratch when a 2-line fix prompt would have
solved it. Token spend in a stuck session can easily 3x a working
session.

Ships: the 12 failure modes (liquid glass not rendering, mobile
broken, video won't load, animations janky, fonts falling back, hover
reveal inverted, Safari vs Chrome diffs, color drift, placeholder
data, rigid output, stuck context drift) with a targeted fix prompt
for each. Plus the meta-rule: after 3 stuck Comments, duplicate the
project and re-prompt. Fighting a session is the #1 way to burn
quota.

Add 11_claude_code_handoff: README template for the Claude Code bundle

Article mentions the handoff README as the artifact that closes the
loop to production, but no template existed. The default handoff
README is serviceable but generic — hand-crafted is the difference
between 'engineering ships this week' and 'engineering throws it out'.

Ships: full README template with production-stack slots, component-
reuse checklist, data requirements, accessibility baseline, explicit
'do NOT do' list, definition-of-done checklist, questions to ask
before coding. Cuts engineering implementation time roughly in half.

Add 10_clarifying_questions: answers cheat sheet for the 9 questions

Article notes that 70% of output quality is set during clarifying
questions, but there was no guidance on what to answer. PMs were
defaulting to "By-the-book SaaS" and "safe" and wondering why every
output looked generic.

Ships: each of the 9 questions Claude asks, with the wrong answer
(what most PMs give) and the right answer (specific, bounded,
opinionated). Includes the 30-second answer template — paste, edit
brackets, go. Single highest-leverage 90 seconds of a Claude Design
session.

Add 09_design_system_setup: the one-hour setup + SKILL.md template

The article dedicates 4 pages to design system setup (§7) but the
repo had zero guidance. This was the gap blocking VPs from rolling
Claude Design out to their teams — no way to make it on-brand.

Ships: step-by-step setup (attach Figma/GitHub/brand assets, validate
in the right order — typography and colors first because that is
where Claude drifts), full SKILL.md template with fill-in-the-bracket
examples for voice/visual/components/illustration, plus the mainten-
ance loop (feed corrections back into SKILL.md, not Comments).

Add 08_stakeholder_prototype: clickable review prototype (article Use Case 4)

Prompt 3 (feature_flow) was doing double duty as both exploratory
prototype and stakeholder-ready review artifact. These are different
jobs: feature_flow is for figuring out the flow with your team,
stakeholder_prototype is for getting a yes/no decision.

This file forces the things stakeholders actually need: real-looking
sample data (no Lorem ipsum), step indicator on every screen, comment-
ready data-element attributes, mobile-responsive, subtle reviewer
hints. Includes the Slack message template to send with the link so
stakeholders actually open it.

Add 07_pitch_deck: slide-deck prompt (article Use Case 2)

Closes the single biggest coverage gap in the toolkit. The article
dedicates a full section to board updates and the slide deck tab but
the repo had no corresponding prompt. Users were mapping a landing-
page prompt (01_investor_demo) to a deck use case and getting poor
fit.

Ships: 14-slide structure with speaker notes, setup checklist for the
Slide deck tab toggles, the 3 fixes that always need to happen on
first generation, honest token cost ($4-7 per deck).

Rewrite README as a serious front door

Persona-driven (who is it for / who it is not for). Quickstart table
mapped to real PM use cases. Explicit article-section → file map so
readers of the newsletter can find what they need. Honest-cost section
up front. Token budget, export paths, and the video workflow summary.

The old README read like a directory listing. This one positions the
toolkit as a daily-reference asset.
Add MIT license

Initial: 6 copy-paste prompts from the Claude Design article

- 01_investor_demo: dark premium liquid-glass demo page
- 02_product_launch: clean SaaS launch / waitlist page
- 03_feature_flow: 4-screen interactive prototype + refinement prompt
- 04_animated_showcase: cinematic video background + Framer Motion
- 05_design_system: CSS primitives, typography, animations, tokens
- 06_pm_tips: six lessons from testing (screenshots, motionsites, modality hierarchy)

Companion repo for the Claude Design deep dive in Product Growth.
